criteria.criterion: In crates/athena-cli/src/main.rs (and any new module), no function exceeds 200 lines; run is a dispatcher of roughly 200 lines or fewer. Check by reading the file.
criteria.evidence: I read the candidate files. `run` in main.rs now spans lines 1018–1152, which is 135 lines, and each arm makes one call to `commands::*`. The longest function in the new commands.rs is `check` at lines 513–607, about 95 lines; every other handler is shorter. No other function in main.rs changed (diff hunks are only at line 6 and inside run).

criteria.criterion: The diff is a pure restructuring: the Command enum, clap definitions, message strings and exit codes are unchanged, and the existing tests in main.rs and crates/athena-cli/tests are not modified or removed.
criteria.evidence: The main.rs diff touches only `mod commands;` (line 7) and the body of `run`. The Command enum and clap derives are untouched. I compared every removed arm with its handler in commands.rs: the message strings, JSON keys, exit codes (0/2/land_pr_code/state.exit_code) and comments are identical. Two cosmetic differences, neither a behavior change: (1) the Hestia Review arm with `unreachable!` became an early `return hestia_review(json)` inside `hestia`, giving the same dispatch; (2) the InterveneArgs and RestartArgs struct literals are now built before `open(true)`, which is pure data construction with no side effects. The stat over crates/athena-cli/tests shows no changes, and the main.rs test module is outside the diff hunks.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-cli`. All existing tests pass, including tests/binary.rs and tests/proposals.rs, which exercise CLI output.
criteria.evidence: Every test binary reported `test result: ok`, with 0 failures in total (for example 126, 187 and 77 passed in the larger binaries; 3 tests ignored in one, and those are ignored at base too since no test files changed). The recorded `cargo test --locked` also passed in CI run 42466071351.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`. Both are clean.
criteria.evidence: Both are cited from Athena's recorded checks for bfaba9e8275a (CI run 42466071351): clippy passed with -D warnings, and fmt --check passed.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo run -p athena-cli -- --help`. The output matches the pre-change output, so the subcommand list is unchanged.
criteria.evidence: The help prints all 36 subcommands plus help (ask … start). I could not build the base side by side because git checkout is not allowed. Instead, the diff shows no change to the Command enum, its doc comments or the clap attributes, which are the only sources of --help text, so the output must match the base.

findings.summary: crates/athena-cli/src/lib.rs is listed as a deliverable (modify) but is not changed.
findings.evidence: `git diff HEAD~1 --stat -- crates/athena-cli/src/lib.rs` is empty. commands.rs is a binary-private module declared in main.rs (`mod commands;`) and uses main.rs helpers through `use super::*`, so lib.rs needs no change. The deliverable is simply unused, not out of scope.

findings.summary: commands.rs imports everything from main.rs with `use super::*`, which couples the two files implicitly.
findings.evidence: commands.rs line 4: `use super::*;`. It works, but explicit imports would show which helpers (open, print_json, show_proposal, …) the handlers depend on.

summary: The change does what was asked. The 549-line `run` in crates/athena-cli/src/main.rs is now a 135-line dispatcher, and the body of each subcommand moved, word for word, into its own function in the new crates/athena-cli/src/commands.rs. The longest new function, `check`, is about 95 lines. I compared every removed arm with its new handler: message strings, JSON keys and exit codes are identical. The clap definitions and all tests are untouched. The only differences are cosmetic: an `unreachable!` Hestia arm became an early return, and two argument structs are built before `open` is called. `cargo test -p athena-cli` passes, and the recorded CI fmt, clippy and test checks pass. `--help` lists the same subcommands; I could not build the base for a side-by-side run, but the help text comes only from the clap definitions, which the diff does not touch. CHANGELOG.md records the change. I found two nits: lib.rs was listed as a deliverable but did not need changing, and commands.rs uses a glob `use super::*`. There is no scope, soundness or behavior problem.
